content.value_statement: Complex development tasks often need clear handoffs between planning, implementation, and verification agents. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for coordinating subagents.
actual_capabilities: Defines five workflow phases: requirements, architecture, implementation, verification, and reflection.
Lists Tier-1 and Tier-2 agent roles for multi-agent development coordination.
Shows Task tool examples for custom Dotagent and built-in Claude Code agents.
Maps supported subagent types to suggested models and purposes.
References workflow state files for main workflow and current phase tracking.
limitations: It only describes workflow conventions; it does not include executable automation.
Referenced agent definition files are not included in this skill package.
It assumes access to the Task tool and compatible subagent definitions.
It does not validate task outputs or enforce workflow state changes.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Plan a feature by assigning requirements, design, implementation, and verification work to focused agents.

use_cases.title: Explore a New Codebase
use_cases.description: Use a focused explorer agent to identify files, entry points, and risks before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Verify Implementation Quality
use_cases.description: Route completed work through QA and verifier roles before marking the workflow complete.

prompt_templates.title: Start A Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agent-workflow skill to break this request into requirements, architecture, implementation, verification, and reflection phases: [task].

prompt_templates.title: Assign Exploration Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the explorer role to inspect [area] and return relevant files, entry points, and risks before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan parallel subagent assignments for [feature]. Include boundaries, expected outputs, and verification handoffs for each agent.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Delivery Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Orchestrate a complete multi-agent workflow for [project change]. Include phase transitions, blockers, verification criteria, and reflection notes.

output_examples.input: Plan a multi-agent workflow for adding authentication to a service.
output: Requirements phase assigns a PM to clarify login methods and security constraints.
Architecture phase compares session, token, and provider integration designs.
Implementation phase splits backend, frontend, and test tasks across focused agents.
Verification phase checks behavior, regressions, and documented handoffs.

output_examples.input: Use explorer before modifying the billing module.
output: Explorer reviews billing entry points, data models, tests, and configuration.
The report identifies safe edit boundaries and high-risk integration points.
Executor uses the report to assign implementation work.

output_examples.input: Set up verification after a complex refactor.
output: QA defines acceptance checks for behavior, tests, and regressions.
Verifier independently reviews the changed paths and reports unresolved risks.
Reflection records workflow issues that should improve the next task.

best_practices: Start with a clear user goal before assigning specialized agents.
Keep each subagent prompt focused on one responsibility and expected output.
Run independent verification before considering a workflow phase complete.
anti_patterns: Do not spawn many agents without clear boundaries or deliverables.
Do not treat planning output as verified implementation evidence.
Do not skip reflection when recurring workflow problems appear.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate multi-agent development workflows across planning, design, implementation, verification, and reflection.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is Markdown guidance and examples for the Task tool.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It declares Read, Task, and Glob as allowed tools.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for custom Dotagent agents and built-in Claude Code agents.

faq.question: Does it include the referenced agent files?
faq.answer: No. It references agent definition paths, but this package only contains SKILL.md.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when a development task needs coordinated subagents or clear phase handoffs.
